info.description:
The Postgres mailing lists and commit history as structured, queryable
data. Every endpoint is `GET` and returns JSON.

The corpus — pgsql-hackers, pgsql-general, and the rest — plus the
`postgres.git` commit log, indexed for full-text search (synonym- and
plural-aware, noise-filtered) and cross-linked: threads to the commits
that landed them, commits to the discussion that shaped them, patches to
their diffstat, GUCs to the release that changed them.

No key required to start: keyless requests are allowed at a low
anonymous tier throttled per client IP — 80 lookups a day, or 16
searches. Register for a key at `/users/register` for the free tier
(10,000 lookups a year, or 2,000 searches) and authenticate with it as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`. The annual budget
and the burst window belong to the **account**, not the key: mint a key
per machine and they all spend from one pool. The year runs from the
account's own anniversary, not the calendar — `x-ratelimit-reset` says
when the pool refills.

The annual budget is spent in cost units, because endpoints don't cost
the same to serve: a lookup costs 1, a keyset listing 2, and `/search`
or `/analytics/*` 5. Every response carries `x-request-cost` with the
price of that route, and `x-ratelimit-remaining` is in the same units. Responses wrap data in a `{ "data": ... }`
envelope; keyset-paginated collections add `next_cursor`/`prev_cursor`
plus `total` (how many rows the filter matched, across every page) and
`total_exact` — `total` is an exact count at or below 10,000 rows and the
query planner's estimate above that, so a large `total` is approximate.
Errors use a `{ "error": { code, message, details? } }` envelope with a
stable `code` slug.

AI agents can use the same data over MCP (Streamable HTTP) at `/mcp` —
same optional keys, same pooled limits; every tool call is charged the cost of
the API route behind it.
info.title: Horton API

get.description:
Messages per time bucket, oldest first. Aggregates the `messages` table directly, so unlike the other analytics endpoints it has no stats-view lag.

The series is dense — a bucket with no messages is present with `count: 0` — and bucketed in **UTC** regardless of server timezone. With `cumulative=true`, `count` is a running total instead of a per-bucket rate.

parameters.description: Bucket granularity. Defaults to `year`.
parameters.name: interval

parameters.description: Lower bound on `sent_at`. ISO-8601 date or datetime.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Upper bound on `sent_at`. ISO-8601 date or datetime.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: When `true`, `count` becomes a running total through each bucket rather than the bucket's own rate. The total starts **inside** the window: a `from` bound does not carry in the corpus-to-date total that preceded it.
parameters.name: cumulative

get.description:
Senders per time bucket of their **first** post, oldest first — the community's expansion curve. `from`/`to` bound that first-post timestamp, so a window selects the senders who *arrived* in it, not everyone who posted during it.

Reads the `sender_stats` view, so it reflects the last pipeline refresh. Same density, UTC bucketing, and `cumulative` semantics as `/analytics/messages`; cumulative here is the distinct-sender total to date.

parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Upper bound on the sender's `first_message_at`. ISO-8601 date or datetime.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: When `true`, `count` becomes a running total through each bucket rather than the bucket's own rate. The total starts **inside** the window: a `from` bound does not carry in the corpus-to-date total that preceded it.

get.description:
Threads bucketed by message count into seven fixed bands (`1`, `2`, `3–5`, `6–10`, `11–20`, `21–50`, `50+`). Every band is always present; an empty one reads `count: 0`.

**`from`/`to` filter `started_at`, but `message_count` is the thread's full lifetime size.** So `?from=2024-01-01` means "threads *started* in 2024, sized by all of their messages — including replies that landed in 2025". It does not mean "messages sent in 2024".

Reads the `thread_stats` view, so it reflects the last pipeline refresh.

parameters.description: Lower bound on the thread's `started_at`. ISO-8601 date or datetime.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Upper bound on the thread's `started_at`. ISO-8601 date or datetime.
parameters.name: to

get.description:
The `limit` senders with the most messages, highest first.

**`message_count` means different things depending on the window.** With no `from`/`to` it is the sender's **all-time** total, read from the `sender_stats` view (and so reflects the last pipeline refresh). With a window it is the count of their messages **inside that window**, aggregated from the `messages` table. Messages whose sender was never resolved are excluded either way.

get.description: Threads, filtered/sorted/keyset-paginated, with per-thread message counts and activity bounds from the stats view (refreshed at the end of each pipeline run). `sort` picks `messages` (message count), `first` (thread start) or `last` (last activity, the default); `dir` (`asc`/`desc`) defaults to the sort's natural direction. `list` keeps threads with at least one message on that list; their counts and activity bounds stay whole-thread. A cursor is bound to the sort, direction **and** list it was minted for — changing any mid-page is a 400. Rows carry their starter message — the durable handle for fetching the thread via `/messages/{message_id}/thread`, since a merge can retire a thread id.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring over the thread subject, or full-text match over any member message (same semantics as `/search`).

parameters.description: Mailing-list name. Keeps threads with at least one message on that list and returns each whole: `message_count`, `started_at` and `last_activity_at` (and so every sort and the `from`/`to` bounds) are whole-thread values, identical to the unfiltered row — unlike `/senders?list=`, which scopes its stats to the list, and `/messages?list=`, which filters individual messages. An unknown name returns an empty page.
parameters.name: list

parameters.description: Sort column: `messages` (message count), `first` (thread start), `last` (last activity). Defaults to `last`.
